newsitem.title: USA: Diagnostic Products sees marketing cost rise.
newsitem.headline: Diagnostic Products sees marketing cost rise.

text.p: Diagnostic Products Corp said Wednesday marketing costs pressured operating income in the fourth quarter and will continue to increase.
The company reported a decline in fourth quarter profits to $0.40 per share from $0.46 a year earlier on a 13 percent increase in sales to $46.9 million.
For the full year, net income was $1.65 per share versus $1.75 in 1995. Sales for the year were $176.8 million, compared with $159.6 million.

"Sales for the fourth quarter and the full year were in line with our internal objectives, reflecting strong growth in our Immulite line of automated immunoassay equipment and reagents and, as expected, declining contributions from our mature line of RIA products," said Michael Ziering, president.
"During the year, we established our own sales and support centers in several countries in Europe and South America.
"We also made a significant investment in pre-launch marketing activity for the Immulite 2000 ... (which) caused operating income to decline as a percent of sales," he said.
"We are on track for launch of the Immulite 2000 during the third quarter of 1997, and expect the new product to contribute to sales growth during the second half of the year," Ziering continued.

"We also expect costs related to product marketing and international expansion to continue to increase, although our objective is to manage these costs to a rate of growth lower than growth in sales." ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
